findings.title: #1173's boot line can be emitted into a black hole and every test stays green — the logger ARGUMENT is unpinned
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Mutating `logBootFlagSummary(createWorkerLogger('[worker]'))` to `logBootFlagSummary({ log: () => {} })` leaves worker/__tests__/boot-flag-summary.test.ts at 9/9. The mutant type-checks (TypeScript accepts a 0-arity arrow where `{ log(message: string, data: unknown): void }` is expected) and no lint rule fires, because `createWorkerLogger` stays imported and used at worker/index.ts:737 and 796. It is not an equivalent mutant: `worker/boot-flag-summary.ts:52-57` states the emitter was split from the builder precisely 'so a test can prove the record actually reaches the log — a correct builder nobody calls leaves #1173 unfixed', and this mutant produces exactly that outcome. It survives because the AST oracle never reads `call.arguments`: it asserts `calls.length === 1`, ExpressionStatement-hood, the enclosing FunctionDeclaration named `main`, block/try ancestry, and try-membership. HEAD's wiring is correct — this is an unprotected regression path, not a live defect, which is why it is ranked P1 and not P0. Closing it is one assertion: `ts.isCallExpression(call.arguments[0]) && call.arguments[0].expression.text === 'createWorkerLogger'`.
